## Rule

**ARC-GEN generator `task_b9b7f026`** (source-read 2026-06-07). 4–7 solid filled
rectangles of **distinct non-black colors (1–9)** are placed (non-overlapping, may
touch) on a black ground. **Only `box[0]`** gets a rectangular **black hole carved
strictly into its interior** (`dwide∈[1,wide-2]`, `dtall∈[1,tall-2]`, offset ≥1 from
every wall → all four walls stay intact; `box[0]` is forced `wide≥3, tall≥3`). Grid
12–18 square. **Output = a 1×1 grid of `box[0]`'s color** = the unique "hollow" box.

In encoded space the target is a **single `1.0` at `output[0, c, 0, 0]`** (everything
else 0; the validator compares in `convert_to_numpy` space, `neurogolf_utils.py:546`).

Cheapest exact formalization (need NOT match LIVE's blend, but happens to be byte-equal):
`argmax_c (bbox_area[c] − count[c])`, channel 0 disqualified.
- solid rectangle → `bbox_area == count` → score **0**
- `box[0]` (rect − interior hole) → `area > count` → score = **hole area ≥ 1**
- background ch0 → huge score → killed by additive `−1e9`
- absent colors → score 0 (< box[0]) → need no penalty

## Algorithm sketch

```
rowsum[c,h] = ReduceSum_w(input)        # [1,10,30,1] cells per row  (the ONE map, 1200 B)
width[c]    = ReduceMax_h(rowsum)        # full WALL row count = box width
count[c]    = ReduceSum_h(rowsum)        # total cells
min_row[c]  = ArgMax_h(rowsum, first)    # wall rows carry the max → first/last = row extent
max_row[c]  = ArgMax_h(rowsum, last)
height_m1[c] = max_row - min_row         # INT64 (height minus 1)
hm1_f[c]   = Cast(height_m1, F32)
area[c]    = hm1_f * width + width       # bbox_area = height*width (no one_f param!)
hollow[c]  = area - count                # bbox_area - count (>0 for hollow, 0 for solid)
hollow_9   = Slice(hollow, ch1-9)        # [1,9,1,1] — exclude ch0 (background)
oh_9       = Cast(hollow_9, to=BOOL)                 # [1,9,1,1] BOOL one-hot (v4: Cast replaces ReduceMax+Equal)
output     = Pad(oh_9, [0,1,0,0,0,0,29,29])         # [1,10,30,30] free graph output
```
Key insight (v4): **Cast(hollow_9→BOOL)** replaces `ReduceMax([1,1,1,1] 4B) + Equal` tail.
Since `hollow_9[c]>0` exactly when ch is hollow (integer area/count sums within F32 precision),
Cast F32→BOOL (0.0→False, nonzero→True) yields the same one-hot. Saves 4 B intermediate `mx`.
Builder: `task291/prototypes/build_task291_slice9_v4.py`.

Key insight (v3): ch0 disqualification via **Slice ch1-9** eliminates `ch0_pen`[1,10,1,1]
(10 params). Area formula `hm1*width + width` eliminates `one_f` (1 param). Shared
`one_i64=[1]` for both Slice starts and Slice axes (saves 1 param). Default Pad fill=False
(no `pad_false` param, saves 1). Builder: `task291/prototypes/build_task291_slice9_v3.py`.

## Cost analysis

Aditya team-best 68 (`Team_Best_Onnx/task291.onnx`, SHA
`b2212d14a2771cebf2412302becf28e9858259ae9b190b0d39951ffdbeaf7644`) =
memory 40 + params 28. It is a 2-node `Einsum -> Pad` graph:
`score` F32[1,10,1,1] costs 40 B; params are `black[10]`, `colors[10]`,
and 4D `pads[8]`.

pad-axes-v1 **66 = memory 40 + params 26**:
- unchanged `score` F32[1,10,1,1] = **40 B**
- unchanged `black[10]` + `colors[10]` = **20 params**
- Pad-18 optional axes: `pads_hw[4]` + `axes_hw[2]` = **6 params**

LIVE 4449 = memory 3516 + params 933.

bbox1map 1756 = memory 1734 + params 22.

slice9-v4 **1737 = memory 1725 + params 12**:
- `rowsum`[1,10,30,1] F32 = **1200 B** (irreducible detection floor)
- INT64 ArgMax extents `min_row`+`max_row`+`height_m1` = 240 B (INT64 by spec)
- F32 scalar chain: `width`,`count`,`hm1_f`,`hm1_times_w`,`area`,`hollow` = 6×40 = 240 B
- `hollow_9`[1,9,1,1] F32 = **36 B** (Slice ch1-9)
- `oh`[1,9,1,1] BOOL = 9 B (Cast F32→BOOL; no mx intermediate)
- params 12 = `ax_w`1 `ax_h`1 `one_i64`1 `sl_ends`1 `pads`8

slice9-v3 1741 = memory 1729 + params 12 (same as v4 except +4 B for `mx`[1,1,1,1] F32)

## Don't-do log

- **Einsum/moment discriminant `D = n³ − RR·CC`** (RR=Σ_h rowsum², CC=Σ_w colsum², both
  free-input self-Einsums → ~356 B total, no [1,10,30] map): **NON-EXACT, discarded.**
  `D` is 0 for solids but its sign is NOT invariant for hollow boxes — **7/8000 fresh
  pairs fail** (winner D went negative, e.g. −1152/−480, so argmax picked a solid). Exact
  `bbox_area = width×height` needs `max` of a row-marginal; Einsum yields only sums, never
  the max. The single `rowsum` map is therefore irreducible.
- **Two occupancy maps `rh`+`ch` (LIVE's 2400 B)** — unnecessary; one `rowsum` gives width
  (ReduceMax), count (ReduceSum) AND extent (ArgMax first/last), because full-width walls
  carry the max rowsum. Do not rebuild the col map.
- **ArgMax directly on `input`** for extent → `[1,10,1,30]` INT64 = 2400 B > the 1200 B
  rowsum. Reduce to F32 marginal first, then ArgMax.
- **BOOL/U8 occupancy to shrink the map** — the FIRST reduction of the F32 input is F32
  `[1,10,30]` = 1200 regardless (ReduceSum/ReduceMax preserve dtype); a Cast only ADDS a
  tensor, and width still needs the F32 rowsum. No win.
- **f16 conversion / spread_scan (21 patterns)** — prior OB_MID_SMALL worker (2026-05-20):
  0 wins, Cast wrapper overhead > savings on a <20k task. Confirmed irrelevant here.
- **INT32 ArgMax (via Cast)** — ArgMax always outputs INT64. Casting min_row/max_row to INT32
  immediately saves 40 B per ArgMax output but ADDS 80 B for the two Cast outputs. Net = 0.
- **Einsum to replace ReduceSum axes params** — Einsum equations are attributes, costing 0 params.
  But: (1) Einsum can't produce keepdims=1 style outputs in a way that avoids Unsqueeze (costs 1 param),
  so net saving is 0; (2) at opset 17, ReduceSum axes as attributes is not supported (removed at opset 13);
  (3) opset 12 (attribute ReduceSum) conflicts with BOOL Pad which requires opset 13+. Dead end.
- **ConstantOfShape for pads** — 8-elem pads initializer (8 params) vs ConstantOfShape(shape=[6],fill=0)
  + [29,29] (4 params): the ConstantOfShape output zeros_6[6 INT64] adds 48 B memory + pads[8 INT64] = 64 B;
  total 4 + 112 = 116 cost, much worse than 8 params. Keep pads as initializer.
- **Opset mixing for attribute-based ReduceSum** — can't mix opset 12 ReduceSum (attribute) with opset 13+
  BOOL Pad in a single-opset-import model. Confirmed: they require different opsets.

## Current floor proof (updated 2026-06-22) — pad-axes-v1 @ 66

The Aditya 68 formulation is already the scalar hollow detector floor for this task:
one `Einsum` computes `rowsum_color[r] * colsum_color[c] * black[r,c]`, with
`colors` killing output channel 0. Its only charged intermediate is `score`
F32[1,10,1,1] = 40 B. The remaining cost is params.

pad-axes-v1 removes the only dominated params in that graph. Pad-12 needs a full
4D pads input `[0,0,0,0,0,0,29,29]` = 8 params. Pad-18 accepts optional axes, so
the same output is `pads_hw=[0,0,29,29]` and `axes_hw=[2,3]` = 6 params. Static
and full-real profile both charge **66**.

**Batch53 re-audit (2026-07-07):** live bar re-verified 66 (profile static=66 profile=66);
floor reconfirmed at the 338-std. Forced-component argument + basis-vector disproof in
`hard_records/sub66_ceiling_audit.md`. Verdict **WALL @ 66**.

Rejected strict-below probes:
- **Free-output basis-vector einsum** (BUILT, batch53): emit `[1,10,30,30]` directly with two
  size-30 corner vectors → 0 intermediates, no Pad, but 60 basis params > (40 B score mem + 6
  Pad params) = +14. Correct (visible 265/265) but dominated. `prototypes/build_task291_basis_freeout_v1.py`.
- No-Pad direct 1×1 output scores 20 but visible is **0/265**; the validator needs
  the full `[1,10,30,30]` encoded output.
- One vector cannot replace both `black[10]` and `colors[10]`: the former selects
  channel 0 at intersections, while the latter suppresses output channel 0.
- A generated fixed top-left mask is dominated by Pad axes; it introduces spatial
  mask memory/params to save at most the 6 Pad params.
